1	# Phase 1 verification — SHA-256 compare of the irreplaceable payload against source.
     2	# Scope: DEV-repo-data (no other copy anywhere), DEV-nonrepo (Baylor OneDrive only),
     3	# DEV-working-tree (uncommitted edits GitHub does not hold).
     4	# repos/ and claude/projects are excluded: independently verifiable vs GitHub / Drive.
     5	#
     6	# VERDICT semantics:
     7	#   MISMATCH   = the SSD copy differs from a source that still exists. Real corruption
     8	#                risk. Fails the run.
     9	#   SOURCE-GONE = on the SSD, absent from source. EXPECTED and not a failure: the SSD
    10	#                is an additive store by design, so it retains files deleted upstream.
    11	#                That is the point — a mirror would have deleted them too.
    12	
    13	$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
    14	# Same SSD root the daily backup writes to, so the two cannot drift.
    15	$dest = (Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'backup-manifest.json') | ConvertFrom-Json).destinations.ssd.root
    16	$dev  = Join-Path $HOME 'DEV'
    17	# Before 2026-10-23 this held Windows paths; on the Mac every tier was skipped
    18	# and the run still printed PASS. An absent SSD is now a FAIL, not a PASS.
    19	if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest)) {
    20	  "VERDICT: FAIL - SSD not mounted at $dest; nothing verified. Plug in CRASHBOX and re-run."
    21	  exit 1
    22	}
    23	$man  = Join-Path $dest 'MANIFEST'
    24	$log  = Join-Path $man 'verify.log'
    25	
    26	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $man | Out-Null
    27	Set-Content -LiteralPath $log -Value '' -Encoding UTF8   # fresh log; the verdict must describe THIS run
    28	function Log($m){ $l="{0} {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'HH:mm:ss'),$m; $l; Add-Content $log $l }
    29	
    30	Log "===== phase1-verify start ====="
    31	$rows = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
    32	$match=0; $mismatch=0; $gone=0; $bytes=0
    33	$mismatchList = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    34	
    35	foreach($tier in @(
    36	  @{ root=(Join-Path $dest 'DEV-repo-data');    label='repo-orphan'  },
    37	  @{ root=(Join-Path $dest 'DEV-nonrepo');      label='non-repo'     },
    38	  @{ root=(Join-Path $dest 'DEV-working-tree'); label='working-tree' }
    39	)){
    40	  if(-not (Test-Path $tier.root)){ Log "SKIP $($tier.label) (absent)"; continue }
    41	  Log "TIER $($tier.label)"
    42	  $files = Get-ChildItem $tier.root -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue

    44	  foreach($f in $files){
    45	    $rel = $f.FullName.Substring($tier.root.Length+1)

    47	    if(-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $src -PathType Leaf)){
    48	      $gone++
    49	      $rows.Add([PSCustomObject]@{ rel=$rel; tier=$tier.label; status='SOURCE-GONE'; sha256=''; bytes=$f.Length })
    50	      continue

    54	      $hs = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $src        -Algorithm SHA256).Hash

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# harvest-dev-docs.sh -- copy every DEV repo's docs/*.md (STATUS, context, handoffs) into
# ~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/<repo>/ so memsearch indexes what Cowork, Codex and Claude Code write into repos.

set -e
if [ -d "$HOME/DEV/KeystoneOS" ]; then DEV="$HOME/DEV"; else DEV="$HOME/Desktop/DEV"; fi
OUT="$HOME/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
n=0
for r in "$DEV"/*/ "$DEV"/Football/*/ "$DEV"/SpecialRequests/*/; do
  [ -d "$r" ] || continue
  name=$(basename "$r")
  case "$name" in _DRIVE|_tools|.claude|graphify-out) continue;; esac
  [ -d "$r/docs" ] || continue
  mkdir -p "$OUT/$name"
  rsync -a --include='*/' --include='*.md' --exclude='*' --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='.venv' "$r/docs/" "$OUT/$name/"
  n=$((n+1))
done
echo "harvested docs from $n repos into $OUT"

content.content:
## Two machines

`stack-check.ps1` tests `$env:OS -eq 'Windows_NT'` and swaps the machine-specific sections. Everything else (memsearch, flush pipeline, memory repos, cloud receipt, context budget, handoff) is shared.

| Section | Mac | Windows laptop |
|---|---|---|
| Jobs | launchd `com.keystone.*` agents | Task Scheduler: `Backup AI Sessions to Drive`, `DailyGmailDigest`, `CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder` (disabled tasks are skipped) |
| venv | `.venv/bin/python` | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` |
| memsearch backend | — | Docker Desktop `milvus-standalone` must be `(healthy)` |
| Backup state | `backup-state.json` (daily-backup) | `backup-ai-sessions-state.json` (daily). `Desktop\DEV` itself is a Drive for Desktop synced root; its weekly robocopy task was retired 2026-09-22 (XML in `~/.claude/scripts/retired/`) |
| SecondBrain | checked | skipped, it is Mac-only |

Windows issue codes:
- `task:<name>`: the last run exited non-zero. `3221225786` (0xC000013A, sleep/shutdown kill) only warns; the age check decides whether the job is really behind.
- `task-stale:<name>`, `task-never-run:<name>`, `task-missing:<name>`: the job is behind, has never run, or was deleted. Tasks live under `\Eric\`. Re-run with `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName '<name>' | Start-ScheduledTask`; a bare `Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName` fails with "cannot find the file specified".
- `task-dual-run:<name>`: a `KeystoneOS-*` task is enabled on Windows. The Mac owns those jobs and the data pulls; disable the Windows copy.
- `milvus-docker` / `milvus-down`: start Docker Desktop; memsearch hooks time out without it.
- `backup-missing:<tag>`, `backup-stale:<tag>`, `backup-error:<tag>`: read `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\05_SYSTEMS\AI_Sessions_Backup\<COMPUTERNAME>\_backup_log.txt`. The script silences robocopy, so re-run the robocopy line in the foreground to see which files failed (codes below 8 are success).

On the Windows laptop the weekly run is Task Scheduler task `\Eric\KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` (Mondays 10:30, pwsh 7). It is the one `KeystoneOS-*` task that stays enabled on Windows.
....
$recent = Get-ChildItem $daily -Filter '*.md' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object Name -Descending | Select-Object -First 3
$flushErr = $recent | Select-String -Pattern 'FLUSH_ERROR' | Select-Object -First 3
if ($flushErr) {
    "FLUSH_ERROR in recent dailies:"; $flushErr | ForEach-Object { "  $($_.Filename):$($_.LineNumber)" }
    $fail += "flush-error"
} else { "recent dailies (3): no FLUSH_ERROR" }

Section "Backup freshness"
$bkState = "$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json"
if ($onWindows) {
    # daily-backup.ps1 (backup-state.json) is the Mac's job; the Windows copy of that file
    # is left over from before 2026-08-14 and says nothing about today. On the laptop the
    # copy is a robocopy job to Google Drive that writes its own state file. Desktop\DEV itself
    # is a Drive for Desktop synced root, not a job; its weekly robocopy was retired 2026-09-22.
    foreach ($b in @(
        @{ f = 'backup-ai-sessions-state.json'; maxH = 50; tag = 'ai-sessions' })) {
        $p = "$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/$($b.f)"
        if (-not (Test-Path $p)) { "$($b.tag): no state file - the job has never finished a run"; $fail += "backup-missing:$($b.tag)"; continue }
        $s = Get-Content $p -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
        $ts = if ($s.finished) { $s.finished } else { $s.lastRun }
        $h = [math]::Round(((Get-Date) - [datetime]$ts).TotalHours)
        if ($h -gt $b.maxH) { "$($b.tag): STALE (${h}h ago)"; $fail += "backup-stale:$($b.tag)" }
        elseif ($s.status -ne 'OK') { "$($b.tag): ERROR ($($s.errors -join ', ')) ${h}h ago"; $fail += "backup-error:$($b.tag)" }
        else { "$($b.tag): OK (${h}h ago)" }
    }
} elseif (-not (Test-Path $bkState)) { "backup-state.json: MISSING (daily-backup has never run?)"; $fail += "backup-missing" }
else {
    $bk = Get-Content $bkState -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
    $ageH = (New-TimeSpan -Start ([datetime]$bk.lastRun) -End (Get-Date)).TotalHours
    # daily-backup.ps1 writes backup-state.json even under -DryRun. A dry run copies
    # nothing, so a dry-run "OK" must never be read as a healthy backup - doing so
    # masks the last REAL run's failure. Observed 2026-08-14: a diagnostic dry run at
    # 20:54 overwrote the 20:38 real-run ERROR and cleared backup-error from this
    # VERDICT while nothing had actually been backed up since the failure.
    # dryRun is a MODIFIER, not a branch: a dry run can also be stale or errored, and an
    # earlier version that returned early on dryRun would report a 40h-old dry run without
6:# $IsWindows does not exist in Windows PowerShell 5.1, so test the OS variable instead.

content.content:
- `lastSeen` advances whenever a conversation's digest is (re)written — this only depends on `history.jsonl`, so it is always safe to advance once the digest reflects the latest prompt.
- `lastFlushed` advances **only on a successful `flush.py` invocation**. If the compiler is unavailable (e.g. its venv is down — a known past failure mode), the digest is still written and the watermark for search still advances, but `lastFlushed` stays behind. The next sync run will retry the flush for that conversation (since `maxTimestamp > lastFlushed`) without re-writing or re-searching anything that hasn't changed.

A conversation with no new prompts past its watermark causes no digest write and no flush call on the next run.

## Scheduling

- On-demand: `.\scripts\keystone.ps1 agy-sync` (supports `-DryRun`, which prints what would be written/flushed and changes nothing).
- Opportunistic: `morning` (and therefore `today`) calls `Invoke-AgySync` as part of its startup, wrapped in try/catch so a sync failure never breaks the morning report.
- Scheduled heartbeat: `scripts\install-agy-sync-task.ps1` registers a Windows Task Scheduler job that runs `keystone.ps1 agy-sync` roughly every 6 hours. Dry-run by default; pass `-Apply` to actually register it. Re-running the installer is idempotent — it removes and replaces any prior KeystoneOS agy task rather than stacking duplicates.

```powershell
.\scripts\keystone.ps1 agy-sync
.\scripts\keystone.ps1 agy-sync -DryRun
.\scripts\install-agy-sync-task.ps1
.\scripts\install-agy-sync-task.ps1 -Apply
```

## Known Tradeoff (Accepted)

Fidelity is prompts plus artifact manifest, not assistant text — the assistant side of a conversation lives only in the protobuf `.db` files, which the bridge chose not to decode for robustness (undocumented schema, high churn risk). Daily-log entries for agy work describe *what was asked and what was produced*, not the agent's reasoning.

# daily-backup.ps1 — KeystoneOS durability automation (macOS port, 2026-08-05)
# Runs daily at 00:30 via launchd agent "com.keystone.dailybackup".
# The Windows original (daily-backup.ps1.win-orig) was removed 2026-10-23; it is in git history.
#
# Jobs:
#   1. Git-sync the memory repos (auto-commit + push).
#   2. Snapshot non-git stores to the cloud targets (rsync, ADDITIVE - no delete).
#   3. Manifest-driven coverage. backup-manifest.json is the single authority.
#
# COVERAGE MODEL — three states, all covered (each gap was a real failure):
#   tracked + committed + pushed  -> GitHub
#   untracked or ignored          -> SSD (captureOrphans)
#   tracked + modified            -> SSD (captureWorkingTree)
# DEFAULT-DENY: a DEV directory absent from the manifest raises an error.
# Never reintroduce repo-detection as a coverage test.

param([switch]$DryRun)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$U = $HOME
# ~/DEV on the Mac, ~/Desktop/DEV on Windows. Resolved the same way as memsearch-sync.js
# (2026-09-30): the hardcoded "$U/DEV" made every Windows run fall back to the 5-path index
# list and report all 52 DEV dirs "absent from disk".
$DevRoot = @("$U/DEV", "$U/Desktop/DEV") | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath "$_/KeystoneOS" } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $DevRoot) { $DevRoot = "$U/DEV" }
$LogDir = "$U/.claude/scripts/logs"
$LogFile = "$LogDir/daily-backup.log"
$StateFile = "$LogDir/backup-state.json"
$ErrorsLog = "$U/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log"
$Errors = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
# Per-copy wall-clock ceiling for Invoke-Rsync's watchdog. Generous: the largest healthy
# snapshot here finishes in seconds, so anything near this is wedged, not busy.
$RsyncTimeoutSec = 900
$Results = [System.Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $LogDir | Out-Null

function Log($msg) {
    $line = "{0} {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss'), $msg
    Add-Content -Path $LogFile -Value $line
#!/bin/bash
# Gate for daily-backup.ps1. Both launchd jobs call it:
#   com.keystone.dailybackup        hourly 12:00-17:00, so a failed try gets another chance
#   com.keystone.dailybackup-login  at login, so a Mac that was off still gets a backup
# Runs the backup only when: no run ended OK today, the Mac is on AC power, no backup is
# running, and fewer than 2 real runs started today (a lasting error must not run 6 times).
# Why daytime + AC: every 21:00 run from 10-13 to 10-22 ended ERROR because the Mac slept
# on battery, and caffeinate -s only holds sleep off on AC (audit 2026-10-22).
# shortcut: checks the log, not a lock file; two runs at the same moment could both start.
LOG="${BACKUP_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log}"
TODAY=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
skip() { echo "$(date '+%F %T') gate skip: $1"; exit 0; }

grep -q "^$TODAY .*daily-backup end: OK" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null && skip "already OK today"
pmset -g ps | grep -q "AC Power" || skip "on battery"
# [.] keeps the pattern from matching any shell whose command line merely mentions the script
pgrep -f "pwsh.*daily-backup[.]ps1" >/dev/null && skip "a backup is already running"
STARTS=$(grep -c "^$TODAY .*daily-backup start (DryRun=False)" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)
[ "${STARTS:-0}" -ge 2 ] && skip "2 tries already today"

exec /usr/bin/caffeinate -i -s /opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh -NoProfile -File "$HOME/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1"

content.thinking:
I'm realizing that even though the harvest logic skips `_DRIVE` by name, bash's glob expansion with a trailing slash still needs to stat each entry to confirm it's a directory — meaning it would follow the `_DRIVE` symlink and stat the Drive root under launchd regardless of the name-based skip.

Stat-ing just the mount point is probably fine since the hang risk is tied to reading or walking files, not a simple stat, though under launchd the macl block might return EPERM instead of hanging anyway. The daily backup already touches Drive through a destination path in its manifest, so this case seems to be handled elsewhere and outside the scope of what I'm checking — I'll move on and check with the advisor before finalizing.
Let me run the verification checks now to confirm everything's correct.

input.verdict: I checked every claim from tonight against the files, logs and launchd state. Most of them hold. The six ops/*.plist files match ~/Library/LaunchAgents byte for byte (cmp), and so does scripts/com.keystone.nightlydigest.plist. Reconcile does run at login (RunAtLoad) and daily at 07:00. Rituals is scheduled Mon-Fri 17:00 plus Fri 15:30, and it is disabled: launchctl print-disabled says so, and STATUS.md:16 dates it 2026-09-24. The bootout/bootstrap commands are valid syntax. The "since 2026-10-08" date matches the work-laptop memory. The KeystoneOS CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md vault paths exist. The old jobs.json regex does throw ("[x-y] range in reverse order", tested in pwsh). The restored one matches the 10-23 cadence OK line and not 10-17. LATEST.md was in fact frozen at "PROBLEM" since 10-04. The RECALL line format matches the job-watch regex. The new stack-doctor sentence matches daily-backup.ps1. The verify-backup tier names match what daily-backup writes. The _INBOX commit's "162 .ps1" is exact. The TOS sibling paths exist. The _INBOX and TOS_Evidence_Brief commits are fine. The real defects: (1) the e16582d commit message puts the start of the meeting-sync outage about seven weeks too late; (2) COMMANDS.md was not updated for verify-backup's new FAIL when CRASHBOX is unplugged, and CRASHBOX is unplugged right now; (3) three docs still point at files deleted tonight; (4) two files edited tonight still carry stale schedule lines. Some claims can't be checked yet. "Keychain works under launchd, tested 2026-10-23" has no scheduled-run evidence: the 10-23 06:01 run still failed, so tomorrow's 06:00 Meeting Sync block is the first proof. Step 2b-harvest has never run in a backup: there is no HARVEST line, and the last backup ended at 22:08, before the commit. The only sync_error ever logged was a transient GraphQL error. So the new "(bad or expired FIREFLIES_API_KEY?)" line in .errors.log will also fire on API hiccups.

defects.defect: The commit message says meeting-sync "had failed every morning since ~09-26". The outage started on 2026-08-06, the Mac's first scheduled run, about 2.5 months earlier. The Tier A memory note written tonight repeats the same wrong date ("~09-26 to 10-23").
defects.evidence: I ran awk over KeystoneOS/outputs/morning/cadence.log, taking the first line after each '== Meeting Sync ==' for every cadence run. 2026-08-04 and 08-05 read 'fireflies-pp-cli not found on PATH; skipped.' Every block from 2026-08-06T07:38 to 2026-10-23T06:01 reads 'Error: not authenticated — set FIREFLIES_API_KEY'. The only successes since the port are two blocks on 09-12, between the 06:00 FAILED line (5815) and the 08:38 cadence OK (6024); neither logged its own cadence line, so they were hand-started. The audit's own pwsh-jobs#0 item says the import 'has not run on the Mac for 2.5 months'. The keystone.ps1 comment ('every morning until 2026-10-23') is consistent; only the commit message and the memory note are wrong.
defects.fix: Before pushing, amend the commit message to read 'It had failed on every scheduled run since the Mac port (2026-08-06) while the cadence logged OK'. Correct the same range in project_fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac.md:156.

defects.defect: COMMANDS.md still offers verify-backup.ps1 as the answer to 'Verify it worked' and 'Did the backup work?'. It doesn't say the script checks only the CRASHBOX SSD tiers, or that it now prints FAIL and exits 1 whenever the SSD is unplugged. The manifest treats the SSD as optional, so this command will report FAIL on a normal day after a clean Drive/GitHub backup.
defects.evidence: verify-backup.ps1:19-22: 'VERDICT: FAIL - SSD not mounted at $dest; nothing verified. Plug in CRASHBOX and re-run.' followed by exit 1. backup-manifest.json ssd: optional:true, 'so an unplugged drive warns instead of fails'. `ls /Volumes` shows only 'Macintosh HD' and 'Recovery', so CRASHBOX is not mounted. COMMANDS.md:467-468 answers '"Did the backup work?"' with just the verify-backup.ps1 command. The last commit to COMMANDS.md (7923a07) predates tonight.
defects.fix: Add one line at both places: verify-backup.ps1 is the SSD integrity check and needs CRASHBOX plugged in, where FAIL with 'SSD not mounted' means nothing was checked, not a bad backup. For the overall answer, point to /backup or backup-state.json, plus verify-drive-backup.sh.
